name: Canton Ashemark
description: Canton Ashemark is a tiny barren body whose surface is a uniform dark grey, scored by impact craters and the subtle striations of solar wind erosion. The body orbits at the edge of a busy shipping lane, close enough to be convenient but too small and resource-poor to attract sustained attention. Its most prominent feature is a smooth-walled crater at the north pole that serves as a natural landing pad, its flat floor the only level ground on the irregularly shaped body.

The airless surface exists in extreme conditions, with sun-facing rock hot enough to burn through standard boot soles and shadowed areas cold enough to freeze carbon dioxide. The low gravity makes surface operations feel like underwater work, every movement slow and every object lighter than expected. The horizon is disconcertingly close, the body's small radius creating a visible curvature that makes the surface feel like the top of a hill in every direction.

An abandoned mining operation occupies the polar crater, its equipment dating to a brief prospecting boom decades ago when helium-3 prices spiked. The operation was small, the deposits modest, and the company folded before extraction yielded a profit. An escape pod debris field scattered across the body's equatorial region tells a separate story: a vessel in distress jettisoned its pods here, and the survivors were recovered, but several pods impacted the surface at terminal velocity and their wreckage has become part of the landscape.

Canton Ashemark's proximity to the shipping lane gives it marginal value as an emergency waypoint, and the abandoned mining infrastructure includes a still-functional communications relay that passing ships occasionally use. The helium-3 deposits, while modest, may become viable again if prices rise. The body's most enduring role is as an accidental memorial: the escape pod wreckage marks the site of a rescue that succeeded, and passing crews who know the story sometimes transmit a brief salute as they pass.
